subject: Defining measurable POC outcomes for HelixGen trial — scoreboard & ownership
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Park <emma@helixgen.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-17T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Defining measurable POC outcomes for HelixGen trial — scoreboard & ownership

Hi Emma — great conversation earlier. Quick post-call recap and proposal for POC success criteria so we can lock the plan before kickoff. Please ping if anything below needs to change.

1) Objective (what success looks like):
- Run a 6-week POC validating HelixGen's clinical note summarization workload on Redwoods' hosted inference.
- Goal: production-feel latency and cost signals + quality comparable to your current baseline.

2) Measurable KPIs (proposed):
- Latency: p50 < 300 ms, p95 < 900 ms (inference path for 512-token summaries).
- Throughput: sustained 50 requests/sec with <20% latency degradation under the above SLO.
- Cost: target average cost <= $0.003/token (end-to-end token accounting we use in our reports).
- Quality: human-eval mean preference >= 85% vs your current summarizer on the 200-case holdout set; ROUGE-L and F1 as automated checks (we'll report both).

3) Data & test plan:
- You to share a 500-sample anonymized workload (attached: helixgen_workload_sample.json) and a 200-sample blind holdout for qualitative review.
- Redwood will run an initial smoke benchmark, then three staged runs (baseline, quantized model variant, caching-enabled variant) with explicit measurement windows.

4) Timeline & cadence:
- Confirm criteria & kickoff: by 2026-05-20
- Data handoff: by 2026-05-24
- Smoke run and tuning: 2026-05-25 — 2026-05-29
- Full evaluation: 2026-06-01 — 2026-06-12
- Readout & recommendation: week of 2026-06-15

5) Ownership (who does what):
- HelixGen: Emma (data handoff, holdout verification), Sam (technical point for integration).
- Redwood (primary owners): Soojin (overall POC lead, readout), Ben (runtime/ops and throughput tuning), Marissa (quality evaluation and human-eval coordination).

6) Deliverables:
- Daily run dashboard (latency/cost/throughput) + weekly readout doc
- Final POC report with cost modeling, recommended deployment config, and gating decision (go/no-go).

Attachments: helixgen_workload_sample.json, redwood_poc_template_v2.xlsx (POC plan template).

Next steps: please confirm by EOD 2026-05-20 and share the anonymized sample (secure link or S3) + any compliance constraints for data handling. Once confirmed we'll schedule the kickoff (30–45m).

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0192

From: Emma Park <emma@helixgen.ai>

Cc: Sam Pennington <sam.pennington@helixgen.ai>
Date: 2026-05-18T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Defining measurable POC outcomes for HelixGen trial — scoreboard & ownership

Thanks Soojin — quick clarifying notes from our side.

• Latency: the p50/p95 targets look reasonable, but we need visibility into the measurement method (client-side vs server-side). Can Redwood provide the exact query and measurement approach so we can align?

• Cost: $0.003/token is ambitious — can you break out the assumptions (model size variant, batching, and if KV cache is counted separately)?

• Data: we'll provide the 500-sample anonymized batch but the legal team needs the handling checklist (S3 permissions, retention, deletion policy). We will also need a data processing agreement signed before the holdout file moves to your environment.

I'll aim to confirm the data handoff date by Tuesday (2026-05-19). If possible, please send the measurement snippet + the PII/handling checklist so I can forward to security.

Best,
Emma

> On May 17, 2026, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > Hi Emma — great conversation earlier...
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Defining measurable POC outcomes for HelixGen trial — scoreboard & ownership

Looping in ops notes and a proposed owner grid for the POC.

- Measurement method: we'll use server-side timing captured at the inference runtime (token emit timestamps) + a small client-side sample to validate network skew. I can paste the snippet into the shared Drive doc.
- Cost assumptions: baseline model = 13B FP16; quantized variant = 13B int8-like; we assume average output length 120 tokens/sample for cost modeling. That gives the $0.003/token target if caching and batching are enabled in production config.
- Security checklist: Marissa to draft the minimal S3 policy and retention/delete TTL; legal will still need to sign DPA.

Proposed owner grid (quick):
- Infra tuning & throughput runs: Ben (ops)
- Human-eval setup & rubric: Marissa
- Billing/cost model: Soojin + Ben

I'll add the measurement snippet and a sample command line for the smoke run to the Drive link.

—Ben

Emma — thanks for the rapid reply and helpful questions. Short answers and actions below: 

1) Measurement snippet: added to Drive link (server-side timing at token emit + optional client check). See: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-HelixGen-POC (shared in metadata).

2) Cost assumptions: Ben's baseline assumptions are in the Drive doc; I'll export a short cost-breakdown table into the POC template and call out which items are controllable (batching, cache TTL, quantization).

3) Security / DPA: Marissa will send the minimal S3 policy and retention language for your legal review by EOD 2026-05-20. For immediate progress we can accept a narrow pre-signed S3 upload/temporary token flow if legal requests to avoid sending the holdout directly.

4) Confirmed next steps:
- Emma to confirm dataset delivery method by 2026-05-19 (you indicated Tues) — if you can't share by then, propose an updated date.
- Redwood to schedule 30m kickoff (ops + data + PM) for the week of 2026-05-25 once data access is cleared.

If that's all good I'll send a calendar invite for the kickoff once I see confirmation from your side.

Cheers,
Soojin
